title: Electrical Circuits & Instrumentation
description: Circuit analysis, analog electronics, filters, sensors, noise, and data acquisition for physiological and laboratory measurement.

modifications: Linked the original DC, amplifier, sampling and sensor lessons to their directly assessed course outcomes. Added a node-voltage calculation for KCL and a direct anti-alias-filter decision item; preserved questions and numeric keys remain unchanged. All scheduled lessons already have expanded or original instructional text, and the package remains partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

prerequisites.statement: Physics: Electricity & Magnetism; Calculus I recommended

outcomes.description: Solve DC networks with Kirchhoff and Thevenin methods.
Analyze first- and second-order transient and sinusoidal frequency response.
Select an amplifier topology for a sensor signal.
Quantify noise, loading, and calibration limits.

lesson_objectives.description: Use nodal analysis for multi-branch networks.
Reduce a source network to Thevenin form.
Apply ideal op-amp assumptions within feedback limits.
Choose an instrumentation architecture for small differential signals.
Compute a first-order RC cutoff frequency.
Explain the Nyquist condition and why it is not enough for real signals.
Model a sensor transfer function and calibration curve.
Propagate uncertainty to a reported measurement.
Analyze a voltage divider and a source with internal resistance using a Thevenin equivalent.
Calculate the loading error when a measuring input of finite resistance is connected, and choose an input resistance that keeps the error below a target.
Compute ADC resolution and convert it into the smallest change in the measured physical quantity, and evaluate which error dominates.
Derive the transfer function of an RC low-pass filter and compute its time constant and cutoff frequency.
Calculate the gain (as a ratio and in decibels) and the phase shift at a given frequency.
Evaluate whether a first-order filter adequately suppresses noise and aliasing for a chosen sampling rate.
Solve two-node resistive current balances.
Determine a port equivalent with a mathematical test source.
Check power conservation and measurement/matching objectives.
Derive a finite-gain negative-feedback response.
Calculate signed input-error and isolated bias-current effects.
Check linear output and input-range assumptions.
Decompose terminal inputs into differential/common-mode terms.
Calculate rejection and interface-imbalance contributions.
Evaluate range and topology-choice evidence.
Calculate first-order frequency and initial-step response.
Compare buffered blocks with a loaded passive ladder.
Distinguish filtering, recovery and clipped information.
Integrate supplied spectral density through a bandwidth model.
Combine variance with explicit covariance assumptions.
Propagate calibration uncertainty and qualify coverage.
Calculate declared ADC bins, codes and reconstruction error.
Check acquisition settling against a stated absolute error target.
Evaluate alias ambiguity and sampling margins.
Recover gain and offset using unsaturated references.
Calculate asymmetric headroom and a separate baseline decay.
Evaluate residuals and conditional diagnostic case evidence.
Analyze a series RLC model using its natural frequency, damping, stored energy and sinusoidal impedance, and interpret its transient, resonance and phase behavior.
Summarize outputs and recover settled affine gain/offset from unsaturated references.
Calculate common-mode rejection and a separately stipulated baseline time scale.
Evaluate clipping domains and conditional diagnostic case evidence.
Analyze an inverting summing amplifier by superposition at the virtual ground and calculate its weighted output.
Calculate integrator and differentiator outputs in time and frequency, and explain offset drift, saturation and high-frequency noise gain and the resistor additions that bound them.
Design first-order active low-pass and band-pass stages and a unity-gain Sallen–Key low-pass from gain, corner frequency and Q, and check the design against the op amp's gain-bandwidth product.

duration.equivalent_structure: Proposed 14-week scope with expanded or original instructional text for every scheduled lesson. Workload and qualified review are absent; no semester equivalence is established.

modules.title: DC network analysis and equivalent circuits

lessons.title: DC network analysis and equivalent circuits
lessons.worked_example: A constructed 12 V source, 4 Ω series resistor and 12 Ω output resistor have Thevenin voltage 9 V and resistance 3 Ω. A 6 Ω load receives 6 V in either the original or equivalent circuit. A 10 kΩ source driving a 1 MΩ meter reads about 99.01% of the unloaded voltage because of loading.

modules.title: Operational amplifiers and analog front ends

lessons.title: Operational amplifiers and analog front ends
lessons.worked_example: A non-inverting stage with Rf=90 kΩ and Rg=10 kΩ has gain 10; a 0.10 V input ideally gives 1.0 V. An instrumentation stage with gain 100, reference 1.65 V and differential input ±2 mV ideally gives 1.45–1.85 V, subject to input, output, bandwidth and noise limits.

lessons.title: Filters, sampling, and anti-aliasing
lessons.worked_example: With R=1 kΩ and C=10 µF, the RC cutoff is about 15.9 Hz and the first-order amplitude ratio at 20 Hz is about 0.622. A 250 Hz cosine sampled at 300 samples/s is indistinguishable from a 50 Hz cosine in its samples, so analog filtering must precede conversion.

lessons.title: Sensors, calibration, and uncertainty
lessons.worked_example: For V=0.50x+0.10 V, a 2.10 V reading gives x=4 units. If voltage standard uncertainty is 0.02 V and calibration parameters are treated as exact, propagated x uncertainty is 0.04 units. For independent I=2.00±0.02 A and R=10.0±0.1 Ω, V=IR has standard uncertainty about 0.283 V.

lessons.title: Reading a sensor without fooling yourself: voltage dividers, loading error and ADC resolution
lessons.worked_example: The divider gives 1.833 V from 3.3 V; a 1 MΩ electrode read by a 10 MΩ input loses 9.1% (and 0.10% at 1 GΩ); a 12-bit ADC on 3.3 V resolves 0.806 mV, or 0.020 °C at 40 mV/°C.

lessons.title: First-order frequency response: an RC low-pass filter for a biological signal
lessons.worked_example: R = 10 kΩ and C = 10 nF give τ = 0.10 ms and f_c = 1591.5 Hz; at 100 Hz the gain is 0.9980 with -3.60° phase, while 10 kHz is attenuated only to 0.157 (-16.1 dB), so a single stage protects poorly against aliasing at 2000 Hz sampling.

modules.title: Nodal networks, port tests and power

lessons.title: Nodal networks, port tests and power
lessons.worked_example: Solve b in terms of a, substitute into a's current balance and recover 3 and 1.5 V. Use branch powers to verify 18 mW source delivery. Suppress only the independent source, apply a mathematical 1 V port test and calculate 1.6 mA for 625 Ω. Predict the added 1 kΩ load voltage and distinguish that measurement-loading calculation from maximum-power matching.

modules.title: Feedback, finite gain, bias and output range

lessons.title: Feedback, finite gain, bias and output range
lessons.worked_example: Use the divider to find β=0.10, then solve the finite open-loop equation before substituting V_in. Compare finite gain with ideal gain and calculate the residual input difference. Isolate the declared positive-input bias drop with its direction, then keep it distinct from offset voltage and the other input's bias effect. Finally check output and both input ranges before relying on linear feedback.

modules.title: Differential signals, common mode and interface imbalance

lessons.title: Differential signals, common mode and interface imbalance
lessons.worked_example: Recover v_d=4 mV and v_c=0.5 V from the two supplied terminals, calculate the three output terms and obtain 0.425 V. Convert the amplitude rejection ratio to 80 dB. For the separate bias-current model, calculate both source drops before subtracting them. Finally check both terminal ranges and output range rather than only the differential amplitude.

lessons.title: Filter loading, baseline and recovery
lessons.worked_example: Calculate both isolated first-order responses at 1 Hz and multiply only under the declared ideal-buffer condition. Derive the passive ladder from its two node equations and compare 1/3 with 1/2 at ωRC=1. For the independent high-pass step, retain the initial transient and evaluate its remaining fraction. Keep these linear calculations separate from a saturated upstream stage.

lessons.title: Noise bandwidth, covariance and uncertainty
lessons.worked_example: Integrate squared first-order response for equivalent noise bandwidth, then multiply its square root by the supplied density. Apply the declared constant gain to RMS, not to variance without squaring. Combine 3 and 4 µV first under independence and then under ρ=0.5 to expose the covariance term. For the separate affine inversion, compute all three sensitivities and recover 0.060 x units.

lessons.title: Sampling, quantization and acquisition settling
lessons.worked_example: Use 1024 equal bins to obtain Δ, take floor for the stated 0.503 V input and reconstruct its bin center. Keep the error sign explicit. For the independent sample capacitor, divide the half-bin target by the full-span step and solve the exponential inequality for 7.624619 µs. Finally compare discrete phase increments for 1300 and 300 Hz and test the exactly half-rate sine.

modules.title: Calibration, clipping, residuals and case evidence

lessons.title: Calibration, clipping, residuals and case evidence
lessons.worked_example: Fit the three unsaturated points to recover G=100 and b=0.10. Compute +9 and −11 mV headroom before interpreting the ±15 mV reports. Compare the five-point compromised fit with interior calibration. For the independent drifting condition, subtract the 0.10 V final baseline and infer the exponential time scale from excess ratios. Use common-mode points to recover the separate leakage coefficient.

modules.title: Second-order RLC transients, damping, resonance and impedance

lessons.title: Second-order RLC transients, damping, resonance and impedance
lessons.worked_example: For R=20 Ω, L=10 mH and C=10 μF, f₀=503.3 Hz, ζ=0.316 and ωd=3000 rad/s. A 1 V step produces about 20.17 mA at 0.50 ms. At 250 Hz the series impedance is approximately 51.96 Ω with phase −67.4°, so a 1 V RMS source gives 19.2 mA RMS and the current leads. A 1 V capacitor state stores 5 μJ. The ideal model omits parasitics and component tolerances.

modules.title: Op-amp summing, integrators, differentiators and active filters

lessons.title: Op-amp signal operations: summing, integrating, differentiating and active filtering
lessons.worked_example: A summer with R_f = 20 kΩ, R₁ = 10 kΩ and R₂ = 40 kΩ turns +0.20 V and −0.40 V into −0.20 V. An integrator with RC = 0.1 s ramps at −5 V/s for +0.5 V input; a 1 mV offset alone would saturate it in about 1000 s unless a 10 MΩ feedback resistor bounds the DC gain at −100. An inverting low-pass with DC gain −20 and C_f = 8.2 nF across 200 kΩ has a 97.0 Hz corner, gain 1.93 at 1 kHz, and a 47.6 kHz closed-loop bandwidth on a 1 MHz GBW op amp.

modules.title: Virtual lab 1: gain, clipping, common mode and baseline recovery

lessons.title: Virtual lab 1: gain, clipping, common mode and baseline recovery
lessons.worked_example: Known interior points recover gain 20 or 100 and settled offset 0.10 V. High-gain ±15 mV inputs clip, compromising an all-point linear fit to gain 70/intercept 0.06. Common-mode references give nominal 80 dB CMRR; a separate baseline condition gives τ≈0.50 s.

grading_policy.attempt_policy: Unlimited formative retries; no summative grade is awarded.
grading_policy.solution_release: Public practice solutions may be shown after an attempt. They are not production exam keys.
grading_policy.late_policy: No deadlines or late penalties exist in this partial package.
grading_policy.appeals: No instructor review workflow is implemented; report ambiguous practice items to repository maintainers.

accessibility.diagram_policy: The seed package contains no imported diagrams; newly authored diagrams require descriptions and individual license tracking.
known_issues: Unicode equations require structured mathematical alternatives and assistive-technology review.

history.summary: Preserved original compact prototype content in separate manifests and readings; labeled partial without semester or credit equivalency.

Added an original lesson on sensor loading and ADC resolution (dividers, Thevenin resistance, input-impedance error, resolution versus accuracy) with synthetic data, formative items with computed keys and retrieval cards. The package remains partial and unreviewed.

Added an original lesson on first-order RC low-pass frequency response, decibels, phase and anti-aliasing with synthetic data, formative items with computed keys and retrieval cards. The package remains partial and unreviewed.

Assessments with items now also list the course outcomes those items assess, derived from each item's lesson objective and that objective's outcome links. The rubric-only case lists none, and neither do the 4 prototype-unit assessments, whose objectives are not yet linked to an outcome. No readings, items or keys changed. The syllabus was regenerated from the manifest: it states the current version, lists every lesson with its item and card counts, and describes the current practice and limitations (it still described only the four original units). The course limitations shown to learners were also updated: they still described one formative check per lesson and the original numerical rules. The package remains partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

Added seven original lessons on nodal/port/power analysis, finite feedback/bias/range, differential/common-mode/interface imbalance, filter loading/recovery, noise/covariance/uncertainty, ADC acquisition/aliasing and calibration/clipping evidence; one synthetic channel-diagnostic lab and a proposed weekly schedule. Developed with Codex assistance. Still partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

Expanded the week-1 DC-network reading with KCL/KVL and unit checks, an open-circuit Thevenin derivation, loaded-port equivalence and meter-loading example. Existing questions, keys and objectives are unchanged. Three compact prototype readings remain; the package stays partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

Expanded the week-4 amplifier reading with inverting and non-inverting gain, instrumentation-amplifier common-mode context, ADC bias and real-device operating limits. Existing questions, keys and objectives are unchanged. Two compact prototype readings remain; the package stays partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

Expanded the week-7 filters/sampling reading with an RC magnitude response, alias equivalence, Nyquist boundary qualification and analog anti-alias filtering requirements. Existing questions, keys and objectives are unchanged. One compact prototype reading remains; the package stays partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

Expanded the week-12 sensor reading with affine calibration inversion, uncertainty propagation, covariance qualification and traceable range/condition reporting. Existing questions, keys and objectives are unchanged. All scheduled lessons now have expanded or original instructional text; the package remains partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

Linked the first four lesson pairs to the course outcomes for DC networks, amplifiers, first-order response and calibrated sensor measurements. Added direct practice for multi-branch node analysis and analog anti-alias filtering; existing questions and keys remain unchanged. The course remains partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

Added an inactive, ungraded end-to-end sensor-channel project draft linking loading, amplifier gain and CMRR, RC response, sampling and ADC resolution under explicit ideal assumptions. The seven-criterion human rubric is unweighted, and the project is not in the assessment schedule. Existing course questions and keys remain unchanged. The course remains partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

Added a second-order series RLC lesson grouped with the existing RC frequency-response reading in week 8. Six numeric and three conceptual items and four retrieval cards cover damping, stored energy, a step transient, impedance, phase, resonance and long-time behavior. The values are synthetic ideal-circuit calculations, not a hardware design; the course remains partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

Added an original op-amp signal-operations reading grouped with the week-5 feedback lesson, following MIT OCW 6.002 Spring 2007 session L22 and recitation R22: inverting summing by superposition at the virtual ground, integrators with offset drift and the lossy-integrator bound, differentiators with rising noise gain and a series-resistor cap, first-order active low-pass and band-pass stages, a unity-gain Sallen–Key low-pass with Q, and the gain-bandwidth/noise-gain limit. Three objectives, thirteen formative items and four cards; the grader accepts kHz. The unit-count limitation is corrected to the bank (13 unit-required items before this release, 20 now). No week was added. The course remains partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

limitations: All scheduled lessons have expanded or original instructional text alongside one synthetic data lab; this is not a full university semester.
The proposed 14-week sequence is unmeasured and unreviewed. Graded homework, exams, a full laboratory sequence and a cumulative graded project remain absent.
New circuits, parameters, references and reports are synthetic; selected linear, clamp, noise and converter models provide no actual hardware or human-subject procedure.

Of 80 numeric items, twenty require units, including four RLC and seven op-amp operations calculations; none checks significant figures or dimensions. Dimensionless ratios and other numeric items ask for bare numbers in stated scales. Choices assess selected circuit/evidence decisions, not diagrams or written diagnosis.
Public keys and feedback remain formative authoring specifications; practice points are not course grades.
Subject-matter, accessibility and workload review remain outstanding; the original text feedback map has a verbal description but no assistive-technology review.
Four primary technical documents were retrieved as link-only references; no teaching text, problem, figure or dataset was imported.
The preserved Nyquist item gives the nominal two-times threshold; exact boundary phase ambiguity, practical filter transition bands and acquisition settling remain separate checks.
intentionally_omitted: Graded assessments, complete laboratory sequence, cumulative graded project, measured workload and qualified human review remain outstanding.
